companyInfo.Footnote: A mutual company, not a stock company. It is grouped with stock companies because it reports according to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.

description: Liberty Mutual sells insurance products and services, including automobile, homeowners, property and casualty, health, and life insurance products. It also provides local underwriting, market knowledge, and services to small commercial customers. As of 2024, the company was the fifth-largest global property and casualty insurer.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
In CEO David Long’s final year at the helm, the privately owned global property and casualty insurer dropped eight spots on the Fortune 500.

  • After Long retired at the end of 2022, the company’s board appointed Liberty Mutual veteran Timothy Sweeney as CEO in January 2023.

  • In 2022, the 111-year-old insurer, based in Boston, saw an 87% decrease in year-over-year profit and a modest gain in revenue of 4%.

  • Liberty Mutual, along with more than a dozen other insurers, continues to push back against the Boy Scouts’ record $2.46 billion settlement of sexual abuse allegations that obligates the insurers to pay what they say are "invalid and questionable claims."

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Headquartered in Boston, Liberty Mutual is the sixth-largest global property and casualty insurer. In 2021, the company recorded 10% year-over-year revenue growth, thanks in part to greater-than-usual growth from its commercial lines.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Liberty Mutual Insurance Group jumps up 16 spots on the Global 500 list this year as the global property and casualty insurer’s revenues inched up 1.3%. Profit, though, told a different tale: Liberty’s net income of $758 million for 2020 marks a 27.4% decrease from 2019’s net. Liberty’s balance sheets were impacted by the pandemic, and the company suffered additional losses owing to the effects of natural catastrophes including Hurricane Laura and the wildfires on the West Coast. Over the past five years, the company’s annual average revenue growth rate has been a solid 2.1%. CEO David Long recently said the firm’s 2020 net income was bolstered by strong investment performance and positive core underwriting results.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Liberty Mutual Insurance Group jumps up six spots on the list this year as the global property and casualty insurer’s revenues inched up 1.3%. Profit, though, told a different tale: Liberty’s net income of $758 million for 2020 marks a 27.4% decrease from 2019’s net. Liberty’s balance sheets were impacted by the pandemic, and the company suffered additional losses owing to the effects of natural catastrophes including Hurricane Laura and the wildfires on the West Coast. Over the past five years, the company’s annual average revenue growth rate has been a solid 2.1%. CEO David Long recently said the firm’s 2020 net income was bolstered by strong investment performance and positive core underwriting results. Founded in 1912, the Boston-based insurer has earned on spot on the list since 1995 and has been a top 100 company since 2007.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: In October 2019, Liberty Mutual fully acquired the global surety and reinsurance operations of AmTrust Financial Services in hopes of becoming a top-three global commercial and specialty lines insurer and reinsurer. But overall it was a tough year on paper. The firm’s profits dropped 52%, which the company attributes to its sale of the Liberty Life Assurance Company of Boston. While Liberty has a well-diversified insurance portfolio, CEO David Long recently warned about the company's exposure to insurance payouts related to the coronavirus outbreak. The chief executive is confident Liberty can ride out the storm, thanks in part to its $1.4 billion cash on hand.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: In October 2019, Liberty Mutual fully acquired the global surety and reinsurance operations of AmTrust Financial Services in hopes of becoming a top-three global commercial and specialty lines insurer and reinsurer. But overall it was a tough year on paper. The firm’s profits dropped 52%, which the company attributes to its sale of the Liberty Life Assurance Company of Boston. While Liberty has well-diversified insurance offerings, CEO David Long recently warned about its exposure to insurance payouts related to the coronavirus outbreak. But Long expects contractual languages in its policies to prevent "material losses." That said, the CEO is confident Liberty can ride out the storm, thanks in part to its $1.4 billion cash on hand.
